name: Split, Croatia

visa.notes: Temporary stay permit for financially independent persons. Digital nomad visa also available.

rent.notes: 2026 aggregator shows 2BR city-centre EUR 850-1,400; Numbeo via Croatia Week put a 2BR centre at EUR 812 in Dec 2024. Typical set for a pet-friendly 2-3BR somewhat outside the centre.

sources.title: Cost of Living in Split 2026 - Freenance
Which is the most expensive Croatian city to live in - Croatia Week

utilities.notes: Electricity and water for ~70 m2 run EUR 120-220 per month, higher with summer AC or winter heating; internet excluded.

sources.title: Cost of Living in Split 2026 - Freenance

healthcare.notes: HZZO (Croatian Health Insurance Fund) universal coverage after temporary residence permit. Private supplementary ~€70-130/mo for expat plans. Anti-VEGF injections available in Zagreb (KBC Zagreb) and Split; covered under HZZO with diagnosis. GLP-1 covered for diabetes indication via HZZO. English availability moderate in major hospitals; better in private sector.

entertainment.notes: Built from fast internet EUR 20-35, streaming, 3-4 dinners for two at EUR 40-70, and gym/activities (EUR 25-40 per person).

sources.title: Cost of Living in Split 2026 - Freenance

phoneCell.notes: National figure: mobile plans EUR 8-18 per line per month, 2 lines.

sources.title: Cost of Living in Split 2026 - Freenance

taxes.notes: Estimated monthly income tax on $72,000/yr household income. Based on jurisdiction's effective retiree rate; excludes sales/VAT/property tax.

medicine.notes: Monthly prescription medication costs for household

healthcare.system: HZZO with KBC Split (Clinical Hospital Center Split) - second largest hospital in Croatia. Good specialist care.
healthcare.prescriptionCoverage: HZZO covers most prescriptions with small co-pays

pros.text: Diocletian's Palace — living in a Roman monument (Historical Complex of Split UNESCO World Heritage, listed 1979)

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List — Historical Complex of Split with the Palace of Diocletian (97)

pros: More affordable than Dubrovnik with better daily infrastructure

cons.text: Winter can feel quiet and grey
Safety & crime: see cited reports for current figures by city and country

taxes.notes: Croatian progressive income tax 20%/30%. Municipal surtax may apply. No US-Croatia tax treaty.
